questions.q: What is published to the Power BI service when you use File → Publish from Desktop?
options: The semantic model (tables, relationships, measures) and any reports built in Report view
The entire Power Query editing history, editable in the service
Only the visuals, without any underlying data
A read-only screenshot of the report
questions.explain: Publishing sends the semantic model and Report-view pages to the workspace. Power Query steps remain editable only in the original Desktop file.

questions.q: What happens when you republish a semantic model that already exists in the workspace?
options: The existing semantic model in the service is replaced with the updated version from your Desktop file
A brand new, separately named copy is always created automatically
Nothing happens until an admin manually approves the change
The service version is untouched; only the Desktop file changes
questions.explain: Republishing overwrites the existing published semantic model with your updated one — which is why Power BI shows an impact-analysis warning before you confirm.

questions.q: Why can having two semantic models with the same name in a workspace cause a publish to fail?
options: Power BI can't determine which one to replace, so it's a best practice to keep names unique before republishing
Power BI automatically merges them, which is always desired
It never causes any issue
It only matters for DirectQuery models, never Import models
questions.explain: Duplicate names in the same workspace create ambiguity for the republish target. Renaming the file, or ensuring only one semantic model shares that name, avoids the failure.

questions.q: What happens to visuals in the service if you rename or delete a column they use, then republish?
options: Those visualizations can break, since they reference a field that no longer exists under that name
Power BI automatically renames the reference in every affected visual
Nothing — visuals are completely independent of field names
The republish is blocked entirely until the visuals are fixed first
questions.explain: Renaming or removing a column or measure that an existing visual depends on can break that visual — this is one of the concrete risks impact analysis is meant to surface before you confirm.

questions.q: What does republishing do to an existing refresh schedule on that semantic model?
options: It triggers an immediate refresh, on top of whatever schedule was already configured
It deletes the refresh schedule permanently
It pauses the refresh schedule for 24 hours
It has no effect on refresh at all
questions.explain: When you republish a semantic model that has a refresh schedule defined, a refresh starts right away as soon as you republish — independent of the regular schedule.
